newsitem.title: UK: UK's Heseltine sees EMU delayed beyond 1999.
newsitem.headline: UK's Heseltine sees EMU delayed beyond 1999.

text.p: European Economic and Monetary Union is unlikely to go ahead in January 1999, British Deputy Prime Minister Michael Heseltine said on Monday.
"It's very unlikely it will emerge on the timescale originally set out in the Maastricht Treaty," he told reporters at the Confederation of British Industry's annual conference.

He added that the Conservative government remained opposed to the EU Social Chapter and a minimum wage and it would continue to fight the EU working hours directive, which says no worker should have to work more than 48 hours each week.
"If and when implemented in full it would go against our national interest," he said.

Heseltine said that even if a European Court ruling on the directive did not go Britain's way, Prime Minister John Major would go to the next European Union intergovernmental conference to ensure it did not have to be applied in Britain.
"That will be a central plank of our negotiating stance," he said.
